title: Siegard delivery graph
description: The derived index of a delivery root. Never authored and never edited: `bin/deliver.py` derives it from the markdown delivery nodes, and `--check` holds a committed copy to them. Nodes are the files; edges are the references their frontmatter and their paths declare. `implements` and `reviews` edges point outside the delivery, at tasks of the work root, and `encodes` edges point past that again, at specification nodes — so a consumer resolving them opens the plan and the specification, not this file. What is delivered is what has a node here; nothing records how far the work has got, and `--outstanding` answers that question from the tasks with no record rather than from a field anybody maintains.

file.description: The node's file, relative to the delivery root. Always `<id>.md`.

task.description: The task this record answers, read from its path. Implementations and proofs only.

unmet.description: The criteria this implementation records as not met, sorted and quoted as the task states them. Omitted when none. It is what the record answered, never a status: nothing schedules from it, and the judgment behind each stays in the record.

ran.description: The passes that ran, in the order the delivery-node contract declares them. Reviews only. A pass absent from this list did not run, and what it wanted is named in the record. This list must hold every value that contract's `passName` allows: a name it accepts and this enum does not would make the derivation refuse an index for a review nobody could have written differently.

unproven.description: The criteria this review's coverage pass found partial, uncovered or unauditable, sorted and quoted. Reviews only, omitted when none. The state of each, and why, stay in the record.

findings.description: How many findings the review recorded. Reviews only, omitted when none. A count for a reader scanning the index — never a score, and no threshold reads it: what a finding costs is in the record, and what it means for the change is a person's.

to.description: A task of the work root for `implements` and `reviews`; an implementation of this delivery for `proves`; a specification node for `encodes`.

at.description: Where the reference sits — the field that declared it, or the path that did. So a reader can open the place a defect names.
